name: Martial arts for kids
summary: How expat parents evaluate taekwondo, karate, judo, BJJ, and kung fu programmes in Singapore — belt systems, sparring safety, and trial norms before prepaid term fees.
body:
Martial arts fill the after-school gap for discipline and confidence, but schools vary wildly in coaching quality and hard-sparring culture. Match art and dojo to your child’s temperament and your school’s CCA load.

## Matching art to child
- **Taekwondo / karate** — kicking/striking patterns, common belt exams
- **Judo / wrestling** — throws and grappling; good for contact confidence without punching focus
- **BJJ** — ground game; check kids-only classes and mat hygiene
- **Traditional kung fu / wushu** — forms-heavy; performance pathways differ

Ask about competition pressure — some families want recreation only.

## Safety and culture
Watch a class: coach attention, bullying norms, and whether belts are earned or sold. Confirm first-aid readiness and concussion/ sparring gear rules. Air-con mats in humid weather still need hygiene standards.

## How to choose
Trial before term packages. Prefer coaches who can explain progression without guaranteeing black-belt timelines. For international-school travel weeks, make-up policies matter as much as syllabus. Girls-only or small-group options exist if that helps settling in.

## Practical tip
Buy only the uniform the school requires after the trial. Fancy weapons or multiple annual grading fees add up — get the extras list in writing with the term contract.
